title: Farm Animal Facts for Kids! Cow, Horse and Pig
description:
Who has a stomach with four parts? Who can sleep standing up? Pick your answer with Milo the bluebird, then find out: a cow chews its cud for a big part of every day, a horse can lock its legs and nap standing up, and a pig digs with its snout to loosen the dirt and cool down.
An interactive animal lesson for kids ages 2-6, with questions to answer, counting, actions to copy, quick checks and a quiz at the end.
facts: Ruminant stomachs have four compartments: the rumen, the reticulum, the omasum and the abomasum; cows may spend 35 to 40 percent of each day ruminating (cud chewing); a cow's salivary glands can make and add 50 to 80 quarts of saliva to the rumen daily; the rumen can hold 25 gallons or more (University of Minnesota Extension, 'The ruminant digestive system', extension.umn.edu/dairy-nutrition/ruminant-digestive-system, read Nov 17 2026).

Horses: the stay apparatus, a complex arrangement of muscles, tendons and ligaments, keeps the legs steady with little effort; in the shoulder a bony groove locks the biceps tendon in place; standing sleep is restful, but horses do lie down for their deepest sleep periods (Kentucky Equine Research, 'Asleep Standing Up: How Do Horses Do That?', ker.com, read Nov 17 2026).

Pigs: the nose serves important functions besides smell; pigs root in soil to obtain iron; older pigs check out a new pig by using their noses to investigate; pigs use their snout to loosen up the dirt and use this newly tilled soil to cool down; sows root to gather materials to build nests (Rutgers 4-H Animal Science, 'Don't Root for That! Why All Aren't Fans of Swine Rooting Behavior', 4hanimalscience.rutgers.edu, read Nov 17 2026).

segments.name: hello
lines: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today we are learning about farm animals!
A cow, a horse and a pig. What can they do?
Three animal friends will show us. Count them with me. One, two, three!
Put on your farm boots. Let's go!

segments.name: cow

lines.t: Who has a tummy with four parts?
Is it the cow? Or is it the lion?

lines: It is the cow!
Here is the fun fact. A cow's stomach has four parts! Four parts, all in one tummy.
Let's count them. One, two, three, four!

lines.t: What does a cow do with its food after it swallows? Hmm.

lines: It brings the food back up, and chews it again! That is called chewing its cud.
Look at the cow, chewing away.
close:cow
Grass goes down, comes back up, and gets chewed again. Chew, chew, chew! Down, up, and chew again.
A cow chews its cud for a big part of every day. Lots and lots of chewing!
The biggest part of a cow's stomach can hold twenty-five gallons or more!
That is a lot of room for grass. Wow! A big, big tummy!
Say it with me. A cow's tummy has four parts!
close:host
Can you chew like a cow? Chew, chew, chew, nice and slow. Chew, chew.
Now say it like a cow. Moo! Moo! One more time. Moo!

lines.t: Quick check! How many parts does a cow's stomach have? Four? Or one?

lines: Four! One, two, three, four. Great job!

short.title: How Many Parts Does a Cow's Tummy Have?

segments.name: horse

lines.t: Who can take a nap, standing up?
Is it the horse? Or is it the monkey?

lines: It is the horse!
Here is the fun fact. A horse can sleep, standing up on its four legs!
Standing still, eyes closed, taking a nap. Shh. Quiet, everyone.

lines.t: How does a horse stay up while it sleeps? Hmm.

lines: Its legs can lock in place, so it stays steady without falling over!
Look at the horse, standing tall.
close:horse
But for its deepest sleep, a horse lies down on the ground. Down it goes!
Lying down, all snug. Sweet dreams, horse! Night, night!
Muscles and strong bands in its legs hold the legs steady, with very little work.
So a horse can rest, and still stand tall. Clever horse! Neigh!
Say it with me. A horse can sleep standing up!
close:host
Can you stand still like a sleeping horse? Stand tall, and lock your legs. Shh.
Now gallop like a horse. Clip, clop, clip, clop! Clip, clop, clip, clop!

lines.t: Quick check! Can a horse nap standing up? Yes, or no?

lines: Yes! A horse can nap standing up. You remembered!

short.title: Can a Horse Sleep Standing Up? Horse Facts

segments.name: pig

lines.t: Who digs in the dirt with its nose?
Is it the pig? Or is it the lion?

lines: It is the pig!
Here is the fun fact. A pig digs with its snout! Its snout is its nose.
Digging with your nose is called rooting. Root, root, root! Dig, dig, dig!

lines.t: Why does a pig dig up the dirt? Hmm.

lines: To cool down! A pig loosens the dirt with its snout, and the soft, cool dirt helps it cool off.
Look at that round, pink snout!
close:pig
Pigs use their noses to say hello, too. When a new pig comes, the other pigs sniff to check it out!
Sniff, sniff! Hello, new friend! Nice to meet you!
A mother pig digs with her snout, to gather things for a cozy nest.
A snout for smelling, for digging, and for saying hello. What a busy nose!
Say it with me. A pig digs with its snout!
close:host
Can you wiggle your nose like a pig? Wiggle, wiggle!
Now say it like a pig. Oink, oink! Oink, oink, oink!

lines.t: Quick check! What does a pig dig with? Its snout? Or its tail?

lines: Its snout! Root, root. Super thinking!

short.title: Why Does a Pig Dig with Its Nose? Pig Facts

segments.name: quiz
lines: Wow! We met three farm friends. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
quiz: Who chews its cud with a four-part tummy?
Who digs in the dirt with its snout?

segments.name: goodbye
lines: You learned so many new things today.
Chew like a cow. Nap like a horse. And dig like a pig!
Which farm friend is your favorite?
Thank you for learning with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
